title: Feasibility study to detect neural markers of psychopathology using ultra high sensitivity PET (dynamic [18F]FDG-PET)
summary:
Positron emission tomography (PET) measures the three-dimensional distribution of a weakly radioactive substance, known as a 'tracer', which has been injected into the body. This substance is a radioactively labelled form of fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG), a sugar variant that accumulates rapidly in tumour cells. However, healthy tissue also naturally metabolises sugar, particularly in the brain. We aim to exploit this fact to develop a new method:
The brain has a high energy turnover and consumes sugar. Depending on which areas of the brain are being used or responding to external stimuli, they consume sugar at different rates. We hope that the highly sensitive PET/CT method will enable us to identify these patterns. We would like to find out whether these patterns develop in response to 'stimuli' (in this case, short film sequences viewed by the patient). This methodology should later help us to identify specific brain patterns in patients with mental illnesses such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, as well as in patients with depression. This could open up new avenues for diagnosing and treating neuropsychiatric disorders.
conditions: This refers to cancer patients for whom [18F]FDG-PET/CT is performed for a clinical reason.

interventions.name: Patients undergoing a clinically indicated static [18F]FDG PET scan will also undergo study-related dynamic PET data acquisition. During dynamic PET data acquisition, patients will be shown short film clips.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Justifying clinical indication for a [18F]FDG PET/CT examination
• Patients with oncological diseases, predominantly lung cancer
• Patients who tolerate a respective lying time of a maximum 60 minutes in the PET/CT scanner
• Age ≥18 years 
• Written consent of the patient
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnant and breastfeeding women
• CNS malignancies
• Psychological disorders such as clinically relevant depression, bipolar disorder etc. 
• Medications related to psychological disorders
• Patients with claustrophobia
• Patients with severely reduced general condition and/or problems/pain when lying on their back, so that extended holding time in the scanner may not be tolerated
• Exclusion criteria according to StrlSchG (such as persons who are placed in an institution by court order or official order)
• Limited capacity of the patient to give consent
